$description: The shared publication corpus. Both test suites read this file and assert the same expected parse — it is what keeps two independent implementations from disagreeing about what correct means.
$doNotEdit: Generated. Change the script, run it, commit the result.
$noHashes: Deliberately records no file hashes or sizes: DEFLATE output differs between zlib builds, so either would make this manifest machine-specific. The archives are committed, so git pins their bytes; this file pins their meaning.

comics.pins: page10 sorts after page9, not after page1
pages order by full path with natural sort, so ch10 follows ch2
ComicInfo.xml, OS cruft and resource forks are excluded from the page list
a ZIP named .cbr opens, because format comes from content not extension
a one-page publication does not divide by zero
a wide image is one spread, not two pages
STORED entries read correctly — a reader must not assume DEFLATE
Zip64 extra fields parse — 64-bit sizes and offsets
the EOCD is found by scanning backwards for its signature, not at a fixed offset
local headers carry zero sizes; the central directory is the only authority
a 2000x3000 page: downsampling and memory-bounded decode have something to do
a truncated archive opens what it can and reports what it skipped
comics.note: The central directory is gone. A reader must not refuse the whole file.

comics.pins: an archive with no images reports zero pages, not an error
a page in a codec nothing decodes is listed and named, and an empty entry is counted as skipped
comics.note: Excluding the JXL entry from the page list would be the easy fix and the wrong one: a page nobody can be told about is a page the reader silently loses.

comics.pins: a RAR4 container opens and its entries keep archive order
a RAR5 container opens; RAR4 and RAR5 are different formats behind one extension
a solid RAR4 is refused by name; libarchive cannot read one at all
comics.expectedRefusal: This comic uses solid compression, which cannot be opened
comics.note: The first entry is not solid, so a reader that delegates straight to libarchive lists page1.png and then fails fatally. Detection must read FHD_SOLID from the headers first.

comics.pins: a TAR container opens; CBT is a supported format, not a mislabelled CBZ
chapter directories inside a TAR order by full path, as they do inside a ZIP
a 7z container is refused by name, not by a generic parse failure
comics.note: Detection fires on the 7z signature before any entry is read, so this fixture carries a valid empty 7z header and no pages.

comics.pins: every ComicInfo field the spec names is read, including a cover that is not page 1

expectedComicInfo.title: The Third Chapter
expectedComicInfo.summary: A summary with an & in it, to prove entities are decoded.

comics.pins: Japanese with no declared direction opens right-to-left
a solid RAR5 parses completely, unlike a solid RAR4
comics.note: Vendored from libarchive 3.8.1's test suite, BSD-2-Clause; see generate.py for why it is not generated. Its entries are .bin, not images, so the page count is zero by design: it pins solid RAR5 parsing and the solid flag, not a solid comic opening.

comics.pins: RAR4 compression decodes to known bytes, not just to the right length
comics.note: Vendored from libarchive 3.8.1's test suite, BSD-2-Clause. Its entries are not images, so the page count is zero by design: it pins decompression against contents known from libarchive's own assertions.

comics.pins: RAR5 compression decodes to known bytes, not just to the right length

ebooks.pins: a valid EPUB 3: mimetype first and STORED, two spine items, a nav document and a cover
an EPUB 2: no nav document, an NCX reached through the spine, and a cover named by a metadata meta
ebooks.note: The two cover conventions and the two table-of-contents formats are the things an EPUB parser most often gets wrong, so both are pinned.

ebooks.pins: a publication's publisher, description and series, stated both the way EPUB 3 defines and the way Calibre made conventional — disagreeing on purpose, so the defined form can be seen to win
ebooks.expectedDescription: A book that states its series twice, and differently.
ebooks.note: `belongs-to-collection` is what the format defines and `calibre:series` is what most files carry; a file with both is a file whose publisher knew better than its converter, so the defined one wins.

ebooks.pins: a fixed-layout EPUB declares rendition:layout, so it is read with the image reader and not offered font controls
ebooks.note: Getting this wrong means offering typography controls for a comic, which `ebook-reader` forbids.

ebooks.pins: a publication that declares no cover takes one from the image its first spine item shows
ebooks.note: The declared cover is what a well-made EPUB carries and what most files do not. A shelf of converted books whose covers are all placeholders is the failure this pins against.

ebooks.pins: an EPUB with no container document is refused by name, not opened empty

audiobooks.pins: an M4B's chapter marks come from the container's own atom
audiobooks.note: MP4 chapter atoms are the form media3 cannot read below 1.11.0, so this fixture is what proves the bump landed.

audiobooks.pins: the same three chapters as ID3 CHAP frames, which are readable without the media3 bump
audiobooks.note: Carried alongside the M4B on purpose: the two containers fail differently and a corpus with only one would hide it.

audiobooks.pins: an audiobook with no chapter markers opens, and nothing is reported as missing
audiobooks.note: Also pins that an .m4a and an .m4b holding the same audio are treated identically — the extension is a hint and the contents are the fact.

audiobooks.pins: a folder of audio files is one audiobook, and part10 sorts after part2
a folder holding both audio and images is the kind the majority of its entries are
audiobooks.note: Two audio files against one image. `publication-formats` requires the app to state which kind it chose rather than choosing silently.

audiobooks.pins: a protected audiobook is refused by name, with no prompt for a key or an account
audiobooks.note: 4 KB of an unencrypted fixture with the ftyp brand rewritten to `aax `. Because the source carries `+faststart`, this stub still holds a valid header and a decodable AAC stream — rewrite the brand back to `M4A ` and ffprobe reads it as aac. That is deliberate: it means the refusal has to come from the **brand**, and a decoder that merely choked on a broken file would not satisfy it. There is no encrypted audio, no key, no account and nobody's recording here, because StoryArc neither implements nor circumvents a content protection.

audiobooks.pins: a truncated audiobook plays what it can and states how much it could not
audiobooks.note: Cut to 60% of the whole, so the header parses and the stream does not finish.

pdfs.pins: a PDF with a real text layer and an outline
pdfs.note: Both platforms must offer selection and search. Only iOS reads the outline; Android hides that control rather than showing it empty (ADR-0011).

pdfs.pins: an image-only PDF reads as a comic on both platforms, with text controls hidden
pdfs.note: No text layer at all, so neither platform may offer selection or search, on any device. Page box is 2:3, matching every other fixture page.

$filenamesNote: Cases for filename metadata inference, which needs no file on disk — it is a pure function over a string. Both platforms assert this same table so neither invents its own idea of what a common naming pattern is. Every value inferred from a filename must be marked inferred, so an authoritative source can replace it later without a conflict prompt.

filenames.why: the common shape: series, zero-padded issue, year in parentheses

a bare number is the whole name. Common inside a per-series folder, where the folder holds the series and the file holds only the issue — so the series is deliberately absent rather than guessed as '003'
volume and issue together, issue marked with a hash
manga chapter naming, and bracketed groups are not part of the title
a spelled-out volume with no issue at all
a series whose own name ends in digits — the parenthesised year is the year, and the title keeps its number
a single volume with nothing to infer beyond the title
a leading zero is dropped, so #01 and #1 are the same issue
a spelled-out chapter, separated by a dash
